result:
The repository has nothing built yet, so I'm staging this from outcomes. Below are the outcome candidates, taken from the spec's Rulings (R1–R11). They're unranked because ranking them is your call. No roadmap text is written yet.

## Outcomes (unranked)

**Track A — Filing-index catalog** (known progression)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index Parquet catalog, with provenance on every row, for the archived quarters in a range you choose | R1, R3 | Request count is small: about 4 quarterly files a year, so ~135 files if you start at 1993, plus listings, under a minute of requests at 3 req/s. Data volume is unknown until I know the size of one file; the probe below would measure it. |
| O2 | Daily indexes added on top of the baseline, catching up after missed days and across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 250 small files a year, one per business day. Cheap. |
| O3 | Stored raw downloads re-parsed after a parser change, with no new SEC requests | R5, R6 | Local compute only. The stage that builds it measures the cost. |
| O4 | Readers see only complete quarter versions, through one active pointer, never half-written files | R9 | Negligible. |
| O5 | Later quarterly corrections recorded as additions and updates; removals held until you approve them by source hash | R7, R10 | Material. A weekly re-read of every supported quarter is the same download volume as O1, every week (§4.2). It also takes your time for each withdrawal approval. |
| O6 | All SEC traffic from this app stays under one shared request budget (3 req/s target), however many workers run | R8 | None beyond the rate limit itself. |
| O7 | Settings validated before any network request, starting from the stated defaults | R11, §4.8 | Negligible. |

**Track B — Managed operation on Azure** (known progression)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O8 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation running on schedules in Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage) | R4 | Azure spend can't be estimated without running it. Track B's core stage would measure it. It also needs your setup time for the subscription and identities. |
| O9 | Alerts, run reports, runbooks and a rehearsed rollback for operating it | §4.7, §8 | Mostly your time. |

**Why two tracks:** every Track A outcome can run locally on real SEC data without any Azure resource. If the tracks were joined, the first usable catalog would wait on ADF pipelines, identities and infrastructure. The two tracks also serve different uses: one is the data, the other is keeping it running unattended. I've proposed both as known progressions because the spec's §7 already lays out their order. Change that if you see an open research question, such as how much the historical index formats vary across your range.

## Choices already made
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
- A uv workspace with four scaffold packages (`sec-edgar-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`, `-ingest`). The spec names only `sec-edgar-ingest`, so which packages hold which code is left to a stage's design.
- The Azure platform. The ADR and the spec are both still **Proposed**, and spec §7 step 1 is to accept them. I'm treating Azure as Track B's platform, not as a settled fact.

## Proposed roadmap file
`specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. The skill uses the spec's filename stem whole.

## Optional probe
To firm up the O1 and O5 volume estimates, I could make two SEC requests: one `index.json` listing for a recent quarter and a size check on its `master.idx`. The SEC requires an identifying User-Agent. If you want the probe, tell me the User-Agent string to send, in organization/name plus contact-email form.

---

**One request:** rank the outcomes within each track and the two tracks against each other. In the same reply, confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the file name. Optionally add a yes/no on the probe (with the User-Agent) and your backfill start quarter if you already know it.
